case: Investigation into alleged 'diplomatic treason' (zdrada dyplomatyczna) over the 2010 Smolensk air-crash investigation
type: criminal investigation (prosecutors' inquiry into the conduct of state authorities)
description: In August 2016, under the PiS government, prosecutors opened an investigation following notifications from Antoni Macierewicz (then defence minister) and the association Solidarni 2010, which accused Tusk, then Prime Minister, and other officials of having knowingly chosen a legal basis for cooperation with Russia on the investigation of the April 2010 Smolensk crash (Annex 13 to the Chicago Convention) that was unfavourable to Poland. The offence of diplomatic treason (Article 129 of the Criminal Code) requires acting to the detriment of the Republic of Poland and carries up to 10 years in prison. The investigation had several threads; according to the reporting consulted, Tusk was never charged in it.
outcome: Part of the investigation was discontinued in March 2026. On 5 August 2026 the National Prosecutor's Office announced that the remaining five threads had been discontinued (decision dated 31 July 2026), concluding after questioning 488 witnesses that no diplomatic treason had been committed: the Annex 13 route was found to have been 'the most advantageous solution' for Poland at the time and there was no evidence that the Prime Minister or other officials acted with intent to harm the state. The decision could still be appealed at the time of reporting. Notes from Poland noted that PiS was expected to dispute the legitimacy of the prosecution service leadership installed under the current government.
presumption_note: Tusk was never charged in this investigation, which prosecutors discontinued for lack of any offence. He benefits from the presumption of innocence; the allegations in the 2016 notifications were never established by any court.
key_facts: Investigation opened on 31 August 2016 after notifications by Antoni Macierewicz and Solidarni 2010
Allegation: choice of a legal framework for the crash investigation that disadvantaged Poland
Partial discontinuation in March 2026; full discontinuation announced 5 August 2026 (decision of 31 July 2026)
Prosecutors found no crime and no intent to harm Poland; decision appealable

case: Investigation into cooperation between the Military Counterintelligence Service (SKW) and Russia's FSB — Tusk heard as a witness
description: Prosecutors investigated former SKW chiefs Gen. Janusz Nosek and Piotr Pytel, who were charged with exceeding their powers by entering into cooperation with Russia's FSB in 2010–2013 without the Prime Minister's legally required consent. Tusk, then President of the European Council, was questioned as a witness at the military department of the District Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw on 19 April 2017 for more than eight hours. Afterwards he described the case as 'highly political' and said he had not invoked his EU immunity. He was separately summoned as a witness in 2017 in the Smolensk crash investigation.
outcome: Tusk testified as a witness only; he was not charged. The charges concerned the former SKW leadership.
court: District Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw, military department (Prokuratura Okręgowa w Warszawie)
presumption_note: Tusk appeared solely as a witness and faced no charges. The former SKW chiefs who were charged also benefit from the presumption of innocence.
key_facts: Former SKW heads Janusz Nosek and Piotr Pytel charged in 2016 with exceeding their powers
Tusk questioned as a witness on 19 April 2017 in Warsaw for over eight hours
Tusk called the case 'highly political'; his lawyer was Roman Giertych

case: Kaczyński v. Tusk — civil defamation claim over the 'serial killers of women' remark
description: PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński sued Tusk over a June 2023 campaign rally speech, given after reports that a pregnant woman had died of sepsis in hospital, in which Tusk said 'today, those in power are serial killers of women'. Kaczyński sought an apology and 10,000 PLN for a charity helping Ukrainian refugees.
outcome: In April 2026 the District Court in Warsaw (judge Tomasz Jaskłowski) dismissed the claim and ordered Kaczyński to pay Tusk 900 PLN in costs. The court found the words were spoken in a political campaign on a contested issue and did not refer directly to Kaczyński, while adding that Kaczyński bore 'moral responsibility' for the tragedies as the political leader behind the abortion-law changes. The sources consulted did not report whether the first-instance ruling was appealed.
court: Warsaw court of first instance (reported by Notes from Poland as the district court in Warsaw)
presumption_note: Civil case in which Tusk was the defendant; the claim against him was dismissed at first instance. No finding of liability was made against him.
key_facts: Remark made at a KO rally in June 2023
Claim: apology and 10,000 PLN to charity
Dismissed in April 2026; Kaczyński ordered to pay 900 PLN costs
